provenance.expert_method:
Where I looked: the room labelled "Multi-Purpose Hall" in the east wing.
Scale: Set scale on the scale bar, 0 to 20 m. Check: the printed 1:200 on A2 gives the same (1 m = 5 mm on paper).
Method: the hall is a plain rectangle. Length tool along the inner face of the walls: 17.84 m × 13.78 m, so the perimeter is 2 × (17.84 + 13.78) = 63.24 m. Then I measured every door opening in the perimeter walls (the gap in the black wall, not the swing arc):
top wall: 2 double doors, 1.72 + 1.70 m
left wall: 1 double door, 1.72 m
bottom wall: 2 double doors on either side of a post, 1.72 + 1.73 m
right wall: double door to the Store 1.72 m, double door to the Servery 1.63 m, single door 0.89 m
total 8 openings = 12.83 m 63.24 − 12.83 = 50.41 m.
Decisions: windows are not subtracted (there is wall below them, so the skirting continues). The zigzag line across the hall is a folding partition, not a wall, so it gets no skirting; the small door at its top end belongs to the partition, not the perimeter. The thin double line on the right wall (≈2.69 m, to the Servery) is drawn like a window, so I treated it as a hatch or glazed screen with wall below and did not subtract it. If it is a full-height opening, the answer is ≈47.7 m. Door reveals (jamb sides) are not added.
Result: ≈ 50.4 m (±0.5 m)
